design.title: Cross-survey latent consistency: the trunk feature of a place must be the same in all three photographs, not three fingerprints that happen to share a label
design.eli5: Last time we showed the model three different photographs of Berlin at once, hoping it would learn what the city looks like. Instead it did the lazy thing: it memorised three separate photo albums and just agreed on the captions. Shown a fourth photograph, it had no album for it and guessed wrong, confidently. This experiment adds a rule during study: when you look at the same street corner in the summer photo, the winter photo and the spring photo, the picture you form in your head has to be THE SAME picture. That forces it to notice the things that do not change between photographs, like the shape of the blocks and the roads, and to stop leaning on the colour of the trees or the shadows that day. A fourth photograph should then look familiar.
design.hypothesis: Experiment 2 produced exactly the clean negative its own pre-registration named: the three training photographs now converge (train_capture_diagnostics 0.060 / 0.053 / 0.088, 94-96% usable on each) while the held-out 2024 photograph barely moved (1.651 -> 1.583, 7% usable, 65% false fix). So 3 MB of weights and a 160-d pooled feature hold THREE separate pixel-fingerprints per 128 m cell with room to spare, and nothing in the current training signal objects: the soft cross-entropy only asks that three different feature vectors all point into the same logit direction, which a linear head satisfies trivially by carving three regions of feature space per cell. A fourth exposure of the same ground lands in none of those three regions, and the fix is confidently wrong. The missing signal is one that acts on the FEATURE the classifier reads, not on the classifier's answer: at every lattice position the paired batch already holds the same ground in all three surveys under one shared heading, so pull each survey's L2-normalised trunk feature toward the stop-gradient mean of the other surveys' features at that position (cosine loss). The classifier then cannot store three fingerprints, because the three must be one vector; whatever survives the pull is the structure the three photographs share (block layout, road geometry, building footprints, water) and the canopy/shadow/colour-balance cues that differ between a summer, a leaf-off and an early-spring survey are penalised. That is the library's L2 entry #1 (cross-survey latent consistency, the top rung of the SSL4EO ladder and the mechanism every cross-date aerial result was trained with), applied directly to the 160-d GAP feature rather than through a projector: a projector would let the feature keep its survey-specific content and discard it only in the projection, which is the opposite of what the linear cell head needs. No VICReg variance hinge: collapse is impossible while a 2,970-way cross-entropy is trained on the same vector. Output-level consistency (KL between the three cell distributions) would NOT work here, because experiment 2 already achieves near-identical argmaxes across the three surveys; the three-fingerprint solution satisfies output consistency perfectly and only feature-level consistency forbids it.
